title: Routing handoff refactor: contracts, microbenchmarks, and predictive regional throttler
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Motivation: The current routing handoff path mixes policy evaluation, regional admission checks, and fallback selection in a single hotpath that is brittle to dependency upgrades and makes performance testing difficult. This ticket decouples the handoff contract by introducing a small, well-documented adapter interface and a suite of contract tests; it also pilots a predictive regional throttler to prevent surge-induced cascading fallbacks.
acceptance_criteria:
1) New RouteHandoffAdapter interface implemented with at least two concrete adapters (lease-free and legacy-compat shim).
2) Contract test suite runs in CI and validates behavior across region affinity/overrides and quota scenarios.
3) Microbenchmark harness shows no regression in median latency and demonstrates p99 improvement under synthetic surge for the new predictive throttler.
4) Incremental rollout knobs (canary % + circuit trip threshold) are available in console and controlled by feature flag.
design_notes:
- Introduce a minimal adapter interface that expresses: evaluatePolicy(input) -> decision, attachLease(decision) optional, and enrichWithRegionalHints(decision).
- Avoid global shared locks in the handoff path; the lease-free adapter uses optimistic stamping and a soft backoff queue.
- Predictive throttler uses a sliding-window estimator (1s granularity) of incoming QPS per region plus downstream capacity signals. It emits soft-throttle hints which the router respects to reduce fallback churn.
tradeoffs:
- Conservative design: keep legacy-compat shim to avoid breaking Dedicated/private customers; this increases short-term code surface but reduces migration risk.
- The predictive throttler favors latency stability over max throughput; in some steady-state high-throughput workloads this may reduce peak utilization.
- Implementing optimistic lease semantics requires careful monitoring; if estimator drifts we provide an immediate rollback path via feature flag.
implementation_plan:
1) Define adapter interface and add lightweight in-process shim (Week 1).
2) Implement lease-free adapter with optimistic stamping + backoff queue (Week 2).
3) Add contract tests and CI jobs that run against a small routing emulator (Week 2–3).
4) Build microbenchmark harness and run baseline vs new adapters (Week 3).
5) Implement predictive throttler and wire into adapter decision path behind FF (Week 4).
6) Canary rollout to 10% of traffic with telemetry dashboards and automatic rollback on error-rate or latency regression (Week 5).
risks:
- Regressing routing p99 under mixed workloads if optimistic path is flawed.
- Contract tests may not cover complex cross-region overrides; we need a follow-up to extend scenarios for Dedicated customers.
- Runtime dependency upgrade (protobufs + routing proto v3) is required; timing must align with infra windows.

2025-09-24: Microbenchmark harness prototype added under tools/routing-bench. Early numbers: baseline p99=42ms, optimistic adapter p99=39ms in no-surge synthetic run (1M requests). Need more representative loads.

2025-09-26: Design review feedback from PM (Aisha Khan) and SRE (Marco Ruiz): add canary rollback metrics and ensure canary uses same regional mix as production. Action: add telemetry filters and canary config in console.
2025-09-30: Contract test job added to CI (routing-contracts) and failing on a race condition around lease renewal; root cause identified and fix in flight (PR #3479).

2025-10-02: Implemented predictive throttler v0 behind feature flag. Local surge test shows p99 improvement during 5x burst: baseline p99=180ms, with throttler p99=95ms. Metrics and dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/route-handoff
